security_audit.summary: All Ruby or shell execution findings are Markdown formatting examples, not executable commands. The hidden-directory references point to documented Claude Code output style locations and are user-visible configuration guidance. remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user confirmation before saving a style under ~/.claude/output-styles, and prefer project-level placement for project-specific behavior.

remediation.suggestion: Label fenced examples as non-executable output style templates to reduce reviewer confusion.

content.value_statement: Claude Code output styles are easy to misconfigure. This skill guides valid style files, placement, activation, and testing.
actual_capabilities: Creates Markdown output style files with required frontmatter fields.
Explains when to keep or remove Claude Code coding instructions.
Guides user-level and project-level output style placement.
Provides naming, description, and formatting rules for style files.
Includes activation and testing steps with the output-style menu.
Uses the included output style reference documentation.
limitations: Does not install or activate styles without file changes in Claude Code configuration.
Cannot override Claude Code tool permissions or security restrictions.
Generated styles still need review for organization policies and safety.
Behavior depends on active Claude Code output style support.

use_cases.title: Team Response Standards
use_cases.description: Create a shared project style that keeps responses consistent for a repository.

use_cases.title: Learning Mode Customization
use_cases.description: Build a style that adds explanations while retaining coding instructions.

use_cases.title: Documentation-Focused Work
use_cases.description: Create a style that emphasizes docs, trade-offs, and structured implementation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Simple Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code output style named Learning Guide. It should explain decisions clearly and keep coding instructions enabled.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Team Preferences
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn these team response preferences into a valid Claude Code output style. Keep coding instructions enabled and include a user-friendly description: [preferences].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Domain Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project-level output style for security review sessions. Preserve security boundaries, keep coding instructions enabled, and include testing steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Existing Style
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this output style for valid frontmatter, clear behavior, safe instructions, and activation readiness. Suggest precise improvements: [style text].

output_examples.input: I need a concise style for bug-fix work.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes a Minimal Fix style with coding instructions enabled, short response rules, and a user-friendly description.

output_examples.input: Our team wants an explanatory review style.
output: Suggests a clear style name and description.
Adds guidance for trade-off explanations and review notes.

output_examples.input: Check whether this style is ready to share.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews frontmatter, naming, safety boundaries, placement, and activation readiness before sharing.

best_practices: Review generated instructions before saving them into user-level configuration.
Use keep-coding-instructions when the style supports software engineering work.
Test each style with representative tasks before sharing it with a team.
anti_patterns: Do not use output styles to bypass tool permissions or security rules.
Do not save broad behavior changes at user level when only one project needs them.
Do not create vague style instructions that conflict with Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates Claude Code output style guidance and Markdown style files with required frontmatter.

faq.question: Does it run commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill references slash commands and file paths, but it does not contain executable scripts.

faq.question: Where can styles be saved?
faq.answer: Claude Code supports user-level and project-level output style directories. Choose project level for team-specific behavior.

faq.question: Can it change security permissions?
faq.answer: No. Output styles change response behavior, not tool permissions or approval rules.

faq.question: Should coding instructions stay enabled?
faq.answer: Enable them for development styles. Disable them only for non-coding roles after review.

faq.question: Does it support Codex?
faq.answer: The marketplace entry supports Codex discovery, but generated files target Claude Code output styles.
